punchline: Surviving six minutes of clinical death didn't give Hal Elrod the life he wanted, but an hour he claimed every morning did.
thirty_sec: Hal Elrod was clinically dead for about six minutes after a drunk driver hit him head-on, and he recovered. Years later he still hit bottom, with debt, falling income and depression. To climb out, he built a morning hour from six practices: silence, affirmations, visualization, exercise, reading and journaling. He says his income more than doubled within about two months, and he started training for an ultramarathon.
question: When you wake up, what gets your attention first: your own goals or someone else's notifications?
